observations.body: With battle turned against him, Moab’s king offers his firstborn heir as a burnt offering on the wall; great wrath comes against Israel, who withdraws.
observations.label: The king of Moab sacrifices his firstborn son

observations.body: The passage presents military defeat, failed breakout, firstborn heir, wall, burnt offering, wrath, and retreat as the scene's observable response or movement.
observations.label: military defeat, failed breakout, firstborn heir, wall, burnt offering, wrath, and retreat

observations.body: The passage places royal child sacrifice beside military defeat, failed breakout, firstborn heir, wall, burnt offering, wrath, and retreat.
observations.label: royal child sacrifice

payload.posture: Read 2 Kings 3:21–27 as evidence about sacrifice, keeping its action, claim, context, and limits distinct.
payload.tension: the source does not identify whose wrath comes or explain how the act changes the battle
